question: What core problem in health economics arises because resources are limited while needs are infinite?
explanation: Scarcity defines the permanent condition where available resources cannot meet all existing human demands and needs. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why must a hospital administration make hard choices about which medical equipment to purchase?

options.A: Equipment manufacturers produce very few items yearly
options.B: Financial funds and physical supplies are limited
options.C: Healthcare workers prefer using older medical machines
options.D: Government rules forbid buying too many new devices

explanation: Limited resources force decision-makers to weigh options and select which purchases provide the greatest benefit. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h1)

question: What term describes the value of the next best alternative given up when making a decision?
explanation: Opportunity cost represents what must be given up to pursue a specific action or investment. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h2)

question: A clinic spends its entire monthly grant on malaria drugs, missing out on buying vaccines. What is the opportunity cost?

options.A: The transport fees for delivering the medicines
options.B: The health benefits lost by not buying the vaccines
options.C: The wages paid to the clinic staff members
options.D: The total financial cost of the malaria drugs

explanation: The forgone alternative represents the true opportunity cost of selecting one good over another. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary driver behind a patient's demand for specific medical treatments?

options.A: The presence of luxury clinic waiting rooms
options.C: The desire to restore or maintain health
options.D: The wish to collect medical supplies

explanation: Healthcare demand is derived demand, meaning people seek services primarily to achieve wellness and recovery. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h3)

question: How does a sudden increase in out-of-pocket user fees typically affect the utilization of routine clinic visits?

options.C: Demand shifts entirely to surgical care

explanation: Higher direct costs discourage patients from seeking non-urgent or routine care due to financial constraints. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which factor directly limits the supply of inpatient hospital care during a personnel shortage?

options.A: Excessive availability of advanced medical equipment
options.B: Low patient turnout at outpatient clinics
options.C: High levels of community health literacy
options.D: Inadequate number of trained nurses and doctors

explanation: Human resources are a critical input; without enough clinical staff, service delivery capacity drops. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h4)

question: What happens to the overall supply of health services when the cost of imported pharmaceutical drugs rises sharply?

options.A: Supply decreases because production and stocking become expensive
options.B: Supply stays stable because medication prices do not affect hospitals
options.C: Supply doubles because patients will demand fewer drugs
options.D: Supply increases because higher prices attract more investors

explanation: Increased input costs make it harder for facilities to maintain previous inventory and service levels. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h4)

question: What entity acts as a third-party payer when a government health insurance scheme covers hospital bills?

options.A: An organization that intermediates between the patient and the provider
options.B: The individual patient seeking outpatient treatment
options.C: The pharmaceutical company manufacturing drugs locally
options.D: The staff nurse managing the hospital ward

explanation: Third-party payers pay providers on behalf of patients, altering how direct prices are perceived. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why might a free healthcare service still carry a significant economic cost for a rural farmer?

options.A: Mandatory fees charged for sitting in the waiting area
options.B: Obligatory purchase of hospital furniture by patients
options.C: Hidden taxes levied immediately after leaving the consultation room
options.D: Lost farming time and travel expenses incurred during the visit

explanation: Economic costs go beyond direct monetary fees to include travel expenses and lost productivity time. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h5)

question: What condition defines market equilibrium in the health sector?

options.C: Supply exceeds demand by a large margin

explanation: Equilibrium is reached when the amount people want to buy matches the amount providers are willing to supply. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is a common result when government price ceilings keep healthcare services artificially below equilibrium price?

options.A: Elimination of all informal out-of-pocket payments
options.B: Shortages and long waiting lists for care
options.C: An immediate surplus of unoccupied hospital beds
options.D: Increased willingness of private investors to build clinics

explanation: Low controlled prices stimulate high demand while discouraging supply, resulting in shortages and queues. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h6)

question: What type of externality occurs when community vaccination programs protect unvaccinated individuals through herd immunity?
explanation: A positive externality delivers unintended benefits to third parties or society as a whole. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why do governments frequently subsidize immunization programs for infectious diseases?

options.A: To punish private clinics for charging high consultation fees
options.B: To reduce the number of trained nurses working in urban areas
options.C: To ensure pharmaceutical companies earn record-breaking profits
options.D: To encourage higher uptake and generate positive community benefits

explanation: Subsidies lower financial barriers, boosting uptake to maximize widespread herd immunity benefits. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h7)
